title: Running the School
answer: Part IV, Running the School, covers teacher planning and grading, assessment and data, operations and finance, and people and leadership. These chapters speak most directly to principals, district leaders, and board members.

children.name: Teacher Planning, Grading, and Feedback
children.blurb: Fifteen teachers in five primary schools in England used AI to help plan lessons for two school terms. Their self reported weekly planning time fell by 52.5 percent, from about 10 hours to under 5 (Carson et al., 2026).

children.name: Assessment, Data, and the Early Warning System
children.blurb: Researchers who build systems to predict student failure found something troubling when they looked closely. A single accuracy number made predictions look more reliable than they were.

children.name: Operations, Facilities, Transportation, and Finance
children.blurb: Boston Public Schools once faced a transportation problem that cost more than $100 million a year. Researchers built an optimization system that redesigned the bus routes, saving about $5 million a year and removing 50 buses while keeping service quality (Bertsimas et al., 2019).

children.name: People, Leadership, and Culture
children.blurb: Researchers interviewed leaders in six Colorado school districts about how they first responded to AI. Some wrote informal guidelines, some banned student use, and some updated their acceptable use policies (McGuire et al., 2026).

sections.body: Running the School is the part of the book that turns to the work of running a school and a district. It covers teacher planning and grading, assessment and data, operations and finance, and people and leadership, though the book's text for this section does not name specific AI actions in these areas. The book says these last four chapters speak most directly to principals, district leaders, and board members. The final chapter states the core argument of the Volume and offers a plan for the first 90 days. A short conclusion then looks back at what the evidence shows and ahead to what may change.
sections.heading: What this covers

sections.body: The book's finding in this part is that the last four chapters turn to the work of running a school and a district. It does not set out, in this section text, separate claims about what works and what does not. The rule it holds to is that these chapters speak most directly to principals, district leaders, and board members. The final chapter states the core argument of the Volume in full and sets out the first 90 days. The conclusion then looks back at what the evidence shows and ahead to what may change.
sections.heading: Where the work stands

sections.body: The pages fit together as the four areas of running a school and a district. A teacher would go to Teacher Planning, Grading, and Feedback for the work of planning, grading, and feedback. A leader would go to Assessment, Data, and the Early Warning System for assessment and data, and to Operations, Facilities, Transportation, and Finance for operations and finance. A leader would also go to People, Leadership, and Culture for people, leadership, and culture. A parent would find that these chapters speak most directly to principals, district leaders, and board members, so the parent's direct entry point is not named in this section.
